sonnet.problem: The story card at card 4 already says both men have a dream on the same night. That gives away the main part of card 8's right answer ('We had dreams and no one can interpret them') and makes the other two answers easy to rule out.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Papa Dorin calls it 'that line again,' but the earlier line was 'The three branches are three days' and this one is 'The three baskets are three days.' The words are not an exact match, so the card points out a repeat that isn't exact.
sonnet.rule: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match. He only points back to words a card has shown.

sonnet.problem: Verse 22, Pharaoh hanging the chief baker, is never told on a story card. It appears only as a vague true/false statement ('just as Joseph described'), so the violent outcome is never told plainly in the BSB's own words.
sonnet.rule: Hard parts. Sexual sin and violence are told plainly in the BSB's own words, like "violated," on a short story card. Nothing is added, and nothing is softened into something the text doesn't say.
